answer: Every agent must lock a stake bond before it can transact. Like building a bridge over a river, crossing costs real capital: identities are cheap to mint, but each one needs its own bonded deposit. If a peer's behavior proves dishonest, the protocol slashes its stake and burns the deposit. An attacker splitting one budget across a meadow of fake identities gains no leverage, because slashing turns any detected fraud into a net loss, making mass identity fabrication a negative-expected-value bet.
